persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Jessica, 34, in Ohio, USA. You look after the house papers for yourself and your mother Linda, who is 70. Every year something is missed: a late fee on the car insurance, a forgotten health insurance deadline. Today you put every important date in one place, so nothing surprises the family again.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Ahead of It, what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Every home has dates that cost money if you forget them. Insurance that must be renewed. A tax that must be paid. A licence that runs out. The dog's vaccine.
They come once a year, at different times, and they all live in one person's head. And heads forget.
Ahead of It holds those dates for you. It shows what is coming next, and what it costs you to miss each one.
Who uses it? The person who carries the household. The app was made in America, so its ready-made list is American.

For example, Medicare. That is health insurance for older Americans, and every autumn there is a short time to change your plan. Property tax is a yearly tax on a house. Car registration is the yearly fee to keep your number plate. Think of your own family's dates too, like insurance or school fees.
Money shows dollars. Think in shillings if it helps.
Everything stays on this phone. There is no bank login, and nothing is sent to anyone.
When you first open it, the app may show a start menu that says What would you like to do. Tap What's coming due to reach the main page.

lines.t: At the top is the name, Ahead of It, and a small word that says all clear, or how many things are overdue.
Under it is the Level line. Level 1 shows only what is next. Level 2 adds the Year map and the Library. Level 3 adds the Hand-off list. Tap change to choose.

lines: The main page is called Next. It has four groups: Overdue, Do something now, Next 90 days, and Later. Each line shows a name, how many days away it is, and a colour.
The colours matter. Red means missing it costs real money. Yellow means a hassle. Green means no big deal.

lines.t: To add the common things quickly, tap the gold button, Quick setup. When the list is empty, it sits inside the big welcome card. Tick what your house has, fix the date on that line, and tap Save my list at the bottom.
To add something of your own, tap the orange button with the plus sign.

lines: A form opens. Write What it is. Choose the Next due date, and how often it Repeats. Choose how bad it is if you miss it. Write who else needs to know, the amount, and where the papers are kept. Then tap Save.
To change an item, tap its name.
When a bill is paid, tap done, with a tick, on its line. The item moves to its next date, so it is ready for next year. At Level 2, the button How also lets you record the amount you paid.

lines.t: Near the top of Next is the money strip. Put amounts on your bills, and it adds up what is due this month and what is paid.

lines: At Level 2, the Year tab shows twelve months on one page, and the Library has 27 ready-made items.
To start again with an empty list, scroll to the very bottom and tap Start fresh, erase this app's data. It asks you twice.
That is all. Put in your real dates, see what is coming, and mark them done when they are paid.
In the test, you will help an American family put their dates in order. Take your time. If something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Jessica in Ohio, sorting out the family's dates. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Any Level is fine. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Ahead of It with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If a menu says 'Good morning. What would you like to do?', tap 'What’s coming due'. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says 'There is nothing saved in this app yet', just tap OK). If a dark screen then says 'Set it up with me — 6 minutes', tap 'I'll explore on my own'. If the 'Good morning' menu shows again, tap 'What’s coming due'. The page now says 'Everything that costs you if you forget it — on one calm page.' (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Linda's Medicare plan (health insurance for older Americans) must be checked every autumn. Add it from the app's ready-made list.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('ahead_v1')||'{}')||{};var it=Array.isArray(d.items)?d.items:[];function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function N(x){var s=String(x==null?'':x).replace(/[^0-9.]/g,'');return s?parseFloat(s):NaN}function MD(x){return String(x||'').slice(5,10)}return it.some(function(i){return /medicare/.test(L(i.n))});}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: The gold ⚡ Quick setup button (or the Library at Level 2) has a ready-made Medicare item. Tick it and save.

tasks.text: The car insurance renews on 1 March and costs $640. If it is missed, the family drives with no insurance, and that costs real money. Put it on the list with the right date, the amount, and how bad it is to miss.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('ahead_v1')||'{}')||{};var it=Array.isArray(d.items)?d.items:[];function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function N(x){var s=String(x==null?'':x).replace(/[^0-9.]/g,'');return s?parseFloat(s):NaN}function MD(x){return String(x||'').slice(5,10)}function car(i){var n=L(i.n);return /(car|auto|vehicle)/.test(n)&&/insur/.test(n)}return it.some(function(i){return car(i)&&MD(i.due)==='03-01'&&Math.abs(N(i.amt)-640)<0.01&&i.sev==='h'});}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Find or add the car insurance item, then tap its name. Check the Next due date (1 March), the Amount, and choose 🔴 Costs real money.

tasks.text: Max the dog needs his rabies vaccine every year on 20 May. Linda's brother Michael must be told about it.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('ahead_v1')||'{}')||{};var it=Array.isArray(d.items)?d.items:[];function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function N(x){var s=String(x==null?'':x).replace(/[^0-9.]/g,'');return s?parseFloat(s):NaN}function MD(x){return String(x||'').slice(5,10)}return it.some(function(i){return /(dog|rabies|vaccin|max)/.test(L(i.n))&&MD(i.due)==='05-20'&&/michael/.test(L(i.who))});}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add it (orange ＋ or the ready-made dog item), set the date to 20 May, and put Michael in 'Who else needs to know'.

tasks.text: The car insurance papers are kept in the blue folder in the kitchen drawer. Write that down so another person could find them.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('ahead_v1')||'{}')||{};var it=Array.isArray(d.items)?d.items:[];function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function N(x){var s=String(x==null?'':x).replace(/[^0-9.]/g,'');return s?parseFloat(s):NaN}function MD(x){return String(x||'').slice(5,10)}function car(i){var n=L(i.n);return /(car|auto|vehicle)/.test(n)&&/insur/.test(n)}return it.some(function(i){var w=L([i.where,i.ref,i.contact].join(' '));return car(i)&&/blue/.test(w)&&/folder/.test(w)});}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Tap the car insurance item's name. There is a box called 'Where the papers / login are'.

tasks.text: The property tax (a yearly tax on a house in America) is $1,850, and Jessica paid it today. Put it on the list and mark it as paid, so it moves on to next time.
tasks.check: (function(){try{var d=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('ahead_v1')||'{}')||{};var it=Array.isArray(d.items)?d.items:[];function L(x){return String(x==null?'':x).toLowerCase()}function N(x){var s=String(x==null?'':x).replace(/[^0-9.]/g,'');return s?parseFloat(s):NaN}function MD(x){return String(x||'').slice(5,10)}return it.some(function(i){if(!/property/.test(L(i.n)))return false;var paid=(i.pay||[]).some(function(p){return Math.abs(N(p.amt)-1850)<0.01});return (i.hist||[]).length>=1&&(paid||Math.abs(N(i.amt)-1850)<0.01)});}catch(e){return false}})()
tasks.hint: Add the property tax with its amount (and make sure it repeats, not 'Once'). Then tap 'done ✓' on its line, or 📘 How → 💵 I paid at Level 2.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: keeps all the important dates that cost money if you miss them in one place
shows what is coming next and how bad it is to miss each one
mark it done when paid and it moves to the next date

daily.task: Add or update a date in Ahead of It — a bill, a renewal or a birthday (made-up is fine).
